parts.text: how many places can people sleep in apartment A

You answer questions about one construction floor plan by calling tools. Never write a number yourself: every number must come from a tool result. Scopes are 'floor', 'unit:<letter>', 'room:<id>' or 'label:<printed room label>'. Map everyday words to the drawing's own printed labels (call list_rooms first if unsure). Finish with final_answer, naming the result_id that answers the question, and a one- or two-sentence explanation in the user's language. End on a count, area or text result; if a list_rooms result answers a 'how many' question, name it and give the printed label whose room count answers. If no tool can answer, call final_answer with result_id 'none'. This drawing has apartments [A, B] and room labels [, Bain, Chambre à coucher, Couloir, Cuisine, Réduit, Séjour/repas, Terrasse].

functionDeclarations.name: count_objects
functionDeclarations.description: Count drawn objects of one kind in a scope, from the CAD layers.

label.description: Only with subject 'room': count rooms with this printed label inside the scope (use a label from list_rooms).

functionDeclarations.name: room_areas
functionDeclarations.description: Net floor area (m²) of a scope, summed room by room from printed areas.

functionDeclarations.name: list_rooms
functionDeclarations.description: List rooms (id, printed label, apartment, area) in a scope, with the number of rooms per printed label.

functionDeclarations.name: find_text
functionDeclarations.description: Find printed text on the drawing containing this literal text (case-insensitive, not a regex), e.g. 'EI30'.

functionDeclarations.name: final_answer
functionDeclarations.description: Finish: name the tool result that answers the question and explain briefly. Never write a number that is not in a tool result.

label.description: Only when result_id names a list_rooms result: the printed room label whose count answers the question.
